statement: A square with side length $6$ is rotated $30^\circ$ about its center. What is the area of the region covered by the original square, the rotated square, or both?

choices.misconception: I found the area of the overlap of the two squares, the region covered by both, instead of the region covered by at least one.
I added only one of the four corner triangles that stick out of the original square, instead of all four.
I assumed the overlap is a regular octagon, as it is for a $45^\circ$ turn, and subtracted that octagon's area, $72\sqrt2 - 72$, from $36 + 36$.
I counted eight protruding corner triangles, four from each square, and added all of them to one square, which counts each piece of the union twice.

hints: The union is the original square plus the parts of the rotated square that stick out.
Each of the four corners of the rotated square pokes out past one side of the original square as a small right triangle with angles $30^\circ$ and $60^\circ$. Find how far the corner pokes out.

A corner is $3\sqrt2$ from the center at angle $75^\circ$, so it sits $3\sqrt2 \sin 75^\circ - 3 = \tfrac{3(\sqrt3 - 1)}{2}$ beyond the side. That is the altitude to the hypotenuse of the protruding $30$-$60$-$90$ triangle.

solutions.reliable: Put the center at the origin with the original square $|x|, |y| \le 3$. A corner of the rotated square is at distance $3\sqrt2$ in direction $45^\circ + 30^\circ = 75^\circ$, at height $3\sqrt2 \sin 75^\circ = \tfrac{3(\sqrt3 + 1)}{2}$, so it pokes $h = \tfrac{3(\sqrt3 - 1)}{2}$ above the line $y = 3$. The rotated square's sides there make angles $30^\circ$ and $60^\circ$ with that line, so the poking piece is a $30$-$60$-$90$ triangle with altitude $h$ to its hypotenuse. Its hypotenuse is $h(\cot 30^\circ + \cot 60^\circ) = \tfrac{4h}{\sqrt3}$, so its area is $\tfrac{2h^2}{\sqrt3} = \tfrac{2}{\sqrt3} \cdot \tfrac{9(4 - 2\sqrt3)}{4} = 6\sqrt3 - 9$. By symmetry there are four such pieces and they do not overlap, so the union has area $36 + 4(6\sqrt3 - 9) = 24\sqrt3$. Transferable idea: union = one shape plus what the other adds; symmetry makes the added pieces congruent.
solutions.elegant: Inclusion-exclusion: the overlap is the original square minus its four poking corners, $36 - 4(6\sqrt3 - 9) = 72 - 24\sqrt3$, so the union is $36 + 36 - (72 - 24\sqrt3) = 24\sqrt3$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
